messages:
alex: quick ping — PR 8642 (adaptive-kernel-scheduler) is ready for review. ran microbench + canary; seeing a p95 bump on longseq. attaching quick numbers below. need 1-2 approvals to merge in today's window. https://git.redwood/pr/8642 :eyes:
priya: can you paste the bench numbers here? CI artifact download is annoying from my laptop.
alex: pasted snapshot from local CI run:
```
baseline (main): p50=12ms p95=120ms p99=210ms throughput=850 tok/s
pr-8642 (adaptive on): p50=12ms p95=129ms p99=235ms throughput=842 tok/s
diff: p95 +7.5% p99 +11.9% throughput -0.9%
```
jamie: hmm p50 unchanged but tail moved. were these runs with kv-cache and microbatching enabled?
alex: yes — kv-cache=on, microbatch=enabled (batch=16), seq=8192, quant=4bit. command used: ```./bench --model=redwood-xt-13b --seq=8192 --batch=16 --kv-cache --quant=4```
mike: did the canary observe the same pattern?
deploy-bot: canary started: pr=8642 region=us-west-2 variant=adaptive-sched (canary id c-4821)
jamie: canary metrics? tail logs?
alex: canary p95 spike mirrors local: dashboard snapshot -> longseq p95 ~ +8% for ~15m after rollout, then settles to +3%. attached small log snippet below.
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:01Z] req_id=... latency_p95=128ms kernel=quant_kv_v2
[2026-03-17T14:14:07Z] req_id=... latency_p95=131ms kernel=quant_kv_v2
```
priya: possible kernel selection or scheduling threshold change. can you run a profile with kernel-level timing? `--profile-kernel` should show if a new kernel path is getting chosen for longseq.
alex: kicked off `./bench --seq=8192 --batch=16 --kv-cache --profile-kernel`; ETA ~6m, will paste when done.
jamie: also try disabling the adaptive threshold in the scheduler to see if that reverts tail. small config flag `sched.adaptive_threshold=false` will test that.
alex: ran both. results below:
```
pr-8642 adaptive=true: p95=129ms p99=235ms
pr-8642 adaptive=false: p95=121ms p99=216ms
kernel-profile (adaptive=true): mostly quant_kv_v2 path at longseq, kernel_time increased ~6ms at tail
```
jamie: that points to the scheduler picking a slightly different kernel sequence under adaptive mode which increases per-token kernel time for long sequences.
mike: if disabling adaptive brings p95 back near baseline, we can merge with adaptive flag off and follow up with a kernel selection fix. timeline ok?
priya: fine with that approach. prefer a short follow-up PR to re-enable with proper kernel guard.
jamie: lgtm once adaptive flag default is false in canary and PR description documents rollback plan. :thumbsup:
alex: updated PR to set `sched.adaptive_threshold=false` by default and added a test plan. https://git.redwood/pr/8642/files
priya: reviewed the diffs, small nit about docstring but not blocking. APPROVED.
jamie: approved. I'll handle the merge once e2e jobs are green. :shipit:
sre-ops: noted — will monitor tail latency and error budget for 60 minutes post-merge. alert rule: runtime.tail_latency.p95 > baseline*1.15 -> paging.
alex: thanks everyone. merging after green e2e, and I'll open follow-up to rework kernel selection logic and add a microbench regression test.
mike: thanks alex — appreciate the quick triage.
jamie: good coordination.
deploy-bot: canary promoted to prod: pr=8642 region=us-west-2
sre-ops: keep an eye on the dashboards for the next hour, I'll annotate the incident timeline if anything weird pops up.
alex: noted, will watch. :eyes:
